subject.title: fix(agents): keep attempts running after auth and MCP fallback failures

question: Should an explicitly configured bundle MCP runtime fail the entire agent attempt on startup/materialization errors, or should selected error classes degrade to core tools?
rationale: Repository policy treats fallback as a product decision, and the patch currently converts all non-abort failures into fail-open behavior without distinguishing transient optional failures from configuration or invariant errors.

options.title: Classify recoverable failures
options.body: Degrade only explicitly recoverable MCP startup failures to core tools while surfacing configuration, permission, and invariant failures as actionable errors.

options.title: Accept broad fail-open behavior
options.body: Treat all non-abort bundle MCP startup and materialization failures as optional, relying on redacted warnings and doctor/probe diagnostics for operator visibility.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Preserve current attempt failure semantics and pursue narrower server-level isolation or preflight diagnostics instead.

recommendation.title: Classify recoverable failures
recommendation.body: Degrade only explicitly recoverable MCP startup failures to core tools while surfacing configuration, permission, and invariant failures as actionable errors.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows broad ownership of embedded attempt orchestration and tool-construction behavior, making this the strongest available routing candidate.
